subject: MSA — allocation of regulatory penalty risk and PCI responsibility

Subject: FinPay redlines to Redwood MSA (liability / penalties)

Vanessa — attaching FinPay's redline of the MSA (see attachment). Two high-level concerns from our legal & risk teams: 1) the Limitation of Liability appears to cap Redwood's exposure in a way that would prevent recovery for statutory/regulatory penalties (GDPR, CCPA, PCI) in the event of Redwood-caused violations; 2) there is ambiguity around third-party claims (PCI assessors, card schemes) and whether Redwood would indemnify those.

Our proposed approach (highlighted in the redline): carve out statutory fines/penalties and third-party regulatory claims from the liability cap; require an express indemnity for PCI-related third-party claims; and confirm that consequential damages remain excluded. We can be flexible on the scope of the carveout if Redwood can accept express fault thresholds (willful misconduct / gross negligence) or provide insurance-backed limits.

Can you route to your legal team? We'd like to lock these points before we finalize the Order Form. Also attaching a short summary of the outstanding procurement conditions.

Attachments: FinPay_MSA_redline_20260518.pdf
--

Team — forwarding FinPay's redlines. Key asks from the customer: uncapped liability for regulatory fines/penalties (GDPR/CCPA/PCI) and an indemnity for third-party PCI claims. Procurement wants a clean Order Form ASAP; we have aggressive revenue commit in this quarter.

Options I see (please advise on preferred guardrails):
A) Full carveout: exclude statutory/regulatory fines from the overall cap; keep consequential damages excluded.
B) Faulted carveout: regulatory fines excluded from cap only where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct caused the regulatory event.
C) Monetary sub-cap: keep overall cap but add a higher sub-cap for regulatory/PCI fines (e.g., 3x annual fees or $5M).

On PCI indemnity specifically: FinPay wants an express indemnity for third-party card brand or acquirer fines/assessments. We could offer indemnity for PCI claims caused by Redwood's breach of PCI obligations, subject to a sub-cap and obligations to mitigate/defend.

Please draft candidate language we can bring to the FinPay call Thursday 11:00 PT. Also highlight any insurance or SOC2 evidence we should share.

Thanks — Vanessa

Vanessa / team — see proposed approach and draft counters below. High-level principles: preserve our standard global cap (fees paid in prior 12 months) and exclusion of consequential damages, but be prepared to accept narrow, faulted carveouts for regulatory penalties where we materially and culpably breach data processing obligations. Also, offer an indemnity for third-party PCI claims limited in scope and amount.

Draft counterpoints (for call):
1) Limitation of Liability: keep overall cap = aggregate fees paid in prior 12 months. Add express sentence: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Regulatory Penalties (as defined below) shall not be subject to this Section 12 to the extent, and only to the extent, they result from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement."

2) Definition — Regulatory Penalties: "'Regulatory Penalties' means fines, assessments, sanctions or similar monetary penalties imposed by a governmental authority arising from non-compliance with data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) or payment card industry rules (e.g., PCI DSS)."

3) PCI / Third-Party Claims Indemnity: offer an indemnity for claims by card brands/acquirers to the extent they arise from Redwood's failure to comply with obligations in the MSA or configuration/processing errors caused by Redwood. Limit the indemnity to direct losses and defense costs and add a sub-cap (suggested: $5,000,000 or 200% of annual fees, whichever is lower). Require prompt notice and control of defense, with our right to participate.

4) Consequential Damages: retain mutual exclusion of consequential, incidental, lost profits, and punitive damages.

5) Mitigation & Insurance: include a clause obligating Redwood to maintain cyber/tech/privacy insurance with commercially reasonable limits; provide SOC2 Type II report and certificate upon request (we can share a link redacted for third parties).

6) Customer remedies for non-culpable regulatory penalties: where a penalty arises without Redwood's gross negligence (e.g., changes in law or customer's misconfig), keep within overall cap and offer cooperation to contest and mitigate.

I'll attach a suggested redline (short counterlanguage) for your call. Happy to tighten numbers if legal ops wants a different sub-cap.

-Rishi

Amelia — thanks for the call today. Per Rishi's notes, here's the pragmatic middle ground Redwood is comfortable with and the language we'll send as a formal counter: 

- Overall cap remains fees paid in prior 12 months.
- Regulatory Penalties (GDPR/CCPA/PCI) will be excluded from the cap only when such penalties arise from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence in performing our contractual obligations.
- For PCI-specific third-party claims (e.g., card brand fines or acquirer assessments) Redwood will provide an indemnity limited to direct damages and defense costs with a sub-cap of $5,000,000.
- Mutual exclusion of consequential damages remains in place.
- Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II report and maintain cyber liability insurance; we'll share redacted SOC2 and insurer details for FinPay's review.

I've attached the proposed counterlanguage (proposed_counterlanguage_20260520.docx) and our SOC2 report. If FinPay's counsel can confirm in principle, we'll incorporate into a clean MSA for signature with the Order Form.
